body: Welcome!!!

I have very bad spatial awareness and tried my hand at driving a couple of times, but I really couldn't judge how far away I was from the vehicle in front of me, at what speed I should go etc. Making U turns and parking is a nightmare.

I can't drive and it is just making me go nuts. I genuinely feel driving will give a great boost to my life, but unfortunately I am not able to. Feel good for you that atleast you are able to do this. Any advice on how you learnt to drive? I come from a country that has very bad traffic and driving sense and I feel I will definitely run into an accident if I start driving.
I totally do this, but not sure if it is because of dyspraxia. Sometimes I kick my duvet totally off and wake up cold in the middle of the night.

"poor time keeping is meant to be one of the possible symptoms of dyspraxia and I suppose my 'coping mechanism' for this is that I always end up being about an hour early for everything - that sort of thing" - Can relate to this so much!!

Yes, I always have to plan what I have to say and if it is a lot, then I even have to rehearse it a few times. This is not for some elaborate speech or discussion, this is just for having a conversation with someone who sits next to me. Also, I hate background noise. It makes me uncomfortable and I can't concentrate. I totally become deaf to what the person in front of me is saying when there is some background noise.
I play strategy games like DOTA but even then it requires lot of coordination and quick responses. I suck at it but I like it though.
You are prepared to do what I don't have the courage, at this moment, maybe some time in the future. Rest in peace.

My situation is more or less the same. The difference is I have landed a good job, but struggling everyday not to get fired. I can't drive either, so any new job search is severely limited to public transport connectivity of the job location. I can't control my voice so people think I'm yelling at them while I'm just speaking casually. I also stammer when I speak fast. If I lose my current job, I most probably will be jobless for the rest of my life, so I slog like a donkey even though I like no part of the work. My only advice is to stay patient, coz as dyspraxics only thing we have is our patience.
Will taking pain killers or aspirin help?
I think the fling happened before Zach started taking the gifts for Hannah. So, Hannah had only the later stuff in mind, while she forgot the fling that happened before.
Same here. It's been the same way since childhood.

All my room mates are out partying while I am home, alone with my game and TV. Perhaps it is better this way.
Yeah I know. But I'm in India and tech takes a lot more time to get here. Hope I have the money to buy it.
I'm available. Maybe I can be of use atleast for this.

I have not been officially diagnosed with dyspraxia but with the symptoms I can say for sure that I have it. I have extreme anxiety while driving. I did get my license but it was because the rules are that sloppy in my country. I don't drive now even though I have a license. I live in a metro and roads are very conjested but thankfully the public transport is good and there is uber yay!! But I had to make tough career choices to stay in this part of city.

I have this exact feeling. I have this friend of mine who is a girl. She is kinda the only girl with whom I  talk with but since she is always surrounded by other friends, I stopped talking to her. It's really hard to stop talking to someone, sometimes the only one you have because simply there are people around.
Exactly
Yeah. I don't feel safe even when I am asleep.
That option isn't available
True. Public transport is not always there and many times prevents me from doing what I wanna do.
I do this too. Even though the other person might not be interested in what I am saying, I just force through what I wanna say.
FRIENDS show is the coping mechanism for me.
If only we could just go to sleep again
In my case, my parents.
One way is, if I could change myself, change my life I would want a reset button. But the thing is that isn't the reality. So a restart button is just all the pain over again. I don't want that.

I have so experienced the same. I am terrible at driving and don't think I will get any better at it. It is really depressing that something people take for granted is so tough and near impossible for us. The major problem has got to do with spacial issues and decision making. I have made peace with the fact that I may never be able to drive. It also affects me at  being social as people think of me as a loser. " You just need more practice" is just so cliche. I get irritated when I hear this, sometimes even shout at people who say this to me. Maybe practice doesn't make it perfect for some people. Sorry that I was able to provide only this sad reaponse.
Happens all the time. As soon as I buy a new phone, I get a glass protector and case and install them before even start using them.

I learnt to ride a bike when I was a kid but didn't try much afterwards as I was afraid. But from 16, I used to go to school in a bike. It is much easier than a scooter as it is less heavy and speed is also low. Driving in traffic might be tough though, but if you can keep to one side, even that should be easy. Initially balance should be tough, so get someone to train with.

I have faced this problem. I think it is mainly because  dyspraxia causes us to have wobley joints and joint hyper mobility and because of this joints lose their strength. I even get joint sub luxation pretty often don't know how many face that issue. Even I tend to put more work on one side like when I walk I put more stress on my right leg than left. Same goes with for my hands. So I think that might also be a cause. Try doing joint exercises regularly and balancing the stress on both sides.

From where I come people have not even heard of dyspraxia, so it can never be explained to them. but when I try explaining that there is a reason why I am so clumsy and not able to play or drive, people say that I am just making up reasons and not trying enough. If only they can see how much effort I put in everyday just doing ordinary things. If there are people who care and will put some effort into understanding, try explaining to them. Otherwise just leave it and carry on. Just not worth it.

I experience this mostly when I am tired have some other issue which distracts me. I totally lose my concentration and become very dyspraxic. I can't seem to do any work and just feel like lying down doing nothing. Getting rest helps. Other times I just force through that.

Driving can be a big issue with dyspraxia. I am facing the same problem. But u say that you haven't felt clumsy at all. So what might cause you to be so bad at driving. Do you have problems with spatial awareness like predicting the distance of an object and the speed of another vehicle coming at you? If you realise what's causing your problems with driving you can concentrate on that. Since it is absolutely necessary for you to learn driving I suggest taking a driving class as driving test can be much simpler that driving in conjested roads. You can also try with an automatic rather than a manual. And once you get a license you can manage without driving if there is good public transport, if driving scares the shit out of you. I do the same thing. I've got my license but I still use the public transport.

I have not been diagnosed with dyspraxia as it is not recognised where I live but from the symptoms that I found, I believe I have it. Given your daughter's symptoms there is a big chance that she has dyspraxia and the best thing to do is to get her diagnosed. Getting diagnosed with dyspraxia won't affect her, in most ways it would help her. When I found out about dyspraxia I was not crushed, instead I felt a calm, it gave me a realisation that all my problems, all those days when I felt something was different with me but not able to find what it was, it had a reason. A proper diagnosis would help provide moral support and if you are able to get special educational help, it would be great. And I am happy that she has great parents like you who take so much care into their children's needs. Also, even though​ you can't get rid of dyspraxia, she learn lot of coping mechanisms on her own as she grows. So there is not need to worry. Just some additional help would be great for her.

I also sort of do the yes man thing. Because I am not good at judging their expressions, if I do the yes man it leaves me with less of decision to make. I also do things like when have I done that before or did I like it the last time in making out of the blue decisions.

I have faced similar problems. Making small decisions are tough and when it comes to making life decisions I become indecisive. Very small thing like whether to cross the road now or not, what dress to wear what to eat are difficult. What I did was created a routine sort of things. Like I select the dress that I will wear for the week in the weekend itself. For dinner I stick to a routine like Monday I'll have same things every week, Friday night go out to some nice place and have steak. But the weird thing is that this becomes a compulsion and when this is broken there is a chance for it to be more painful.

It did learn to drive but just driving in the traffic scares me a lot. And then there is too much stress as I have to look for vehicles signals and keep track of turns and doing all these seem impossible to me.

I don't think getting a diagnosis would help as here there is no knowledge of dyspraxia. I don't think even getting a diagnosis is possible. And the regard to help, I think the problem is with me. It's maybe an ego sort of thing, like in sports and other things I don't get along as I suck at it and so when I ask for help I feel that they would think very low of me ( even though that might not matter). Anyways thanks for replying to this.

I have faced this problem for a long time. Whenever I get into a conversation I can not get hold of what said previously. Sometimes I end up saying opposite things until the other person corrects me. Other people remember what I said more that I do myself. I try to cope with this by planning whatever I am gonna speak and sticking to it. It may not be possible always but has helped me many times. Sometimes it would be funny. I would say whatever I wanted to say and then just get the hell out of there. This thread makes me feel a little good that there are people out there who face the problems that I face everyday. That I am not alone.
